findings.title: Stored XSS via URLField in Django admin — removal of URL scheme validation (CVE-2026-15920 regression)
findings.description: The diff removes the URLValidator-based scheme check that previously prevented dangerous URL schemes (e.g., `javascript:`, `data:`) from being rendered as clickable links in the Django admin. Without this guard, a stored URLField value such as `javascript:alert(document.cookie)` is rendered verbatim into the `href` attribute via `format_html('{}', value, value)`. Because `format_html` only HTML-escapes the value (and `javascript:alert(1)` contains no HTML-special characters), the resulting markup is `…`. When an authenticated admin user clicks the link on a changelist or read-only field view, the script executes in the admin's origin, enabling session-token theft, CSRF, or further admin-panel manipulation. This is a regression that re-introduces CVE-2026-15920.
